generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: INSIDE THE LOOP: FIVE AI ATTACK FRAMEWORKS THAT NEVER ASK PERMISSION
Summary: Elastic analyzed five agentic offensive frameworks: ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI, and HexStrike. These tools let an LLM drive scanners, shells, and cloud CLIs in bursts of two to 25 seconds. None of them enforce authorization in code, and ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI switch to new proxies and User-Agents when blocked. GTIG and Mandiant have already seen four of them in real intrusions, and Microsoft has linked ARTEX to Storm-0940. Defenders should choose ahead of time which detections can trigger automatic containment. Defenders should also pair IP blocks with token and session revocation, and track how quickly each identity acts and in what order across sessions rather than relying on framework fingerprints, which Elastic's own ES|QL hunt only partly addresses.

Editorial idea:
AI-powered offensive frameworks can move through cyber operations without waiting for authorization, forcing defenders to replace reactive review with automatic boundaries and containment.

Central subject:
The accelerating autonomy of AI-driven cyberattacks versus defender control.

Visual relationship:
An attacker’s automated sequence advances continuously while the defender’s safeguards must identify, authorize, and stop each action under pressure.

Composition:
A narrow defensive checkpoint sits across a branching operational path. Several anonymous machine-directed traces approach from one side, while the checkpoint contains a few clear intervention points and a sealed emergency stop at the center. The composition should emphasize speed pressing against deliberate control, without depicting a literal interface.

Permitted literal elements:
A physical checkpoint or gate
Multiple advancing paths converging on the checkpoint
A visible emergency stop mechanism
A few distinct intervention barriers
An empty surrounding environment suggesting institutional distance

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
artist imitation
rendered text
logos
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting generic hackers or computers instead of autonomous attack sequences
Making the defensive checkpoint look effortless or fully secure
Using decorative cyber or AI imagery without showing the tension between speed and authorization
Adding labels, interface text, logos, or unexplained hardware

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
